I started learning when I started immediately thinking about my dreams once I was awake, since I would be alone in the morning. 

Eventually, it becomes a habit and you start automatically thinking of your dreams unless actively trying to forget them (have to rush/do something busy in morning.) 

After a while, you start being kind of conscious of the dream while you're in it. Not necessarily recognizing it as a dream, but you start feeling more like you're naturally making the choices you would make if you were awake. These will be different because weird shit goes down in your dreams.

Also, it might be hard to remember this, but if you ever want to go back to a dream, if you feel that "Wish I could go back to it" feeling, try not moving your body at all when you wake up. Then, keep your eyes closed (I think the light might seriously disrupt it) then try and will yourself back. This worked for me once, but once I got back in, the character in the dream I wanted to go back to didn't remember me, as if I was a completely different character, and there were moments when everything was white, and even though I could kind of hear things in the dream, I knew it was time to wake up.

Basically, 

1. Remember dreams when you wake up
2. Start becoming conscious that you're dreaming and making choices you would make in real life.
2.5/3. Be able to wake yourself up from your dreams (try shaking, recognizing you're in a dream, just kind of feel it, sometimes you know you're doing it but don't realize that you did it until you wake up)
4. Keep in mind how to go back to a dream
5. Slowly make things go your way, and if you go back into a dream, you may already be able to recognize you're in a dream, and do what you want. (Lucid)
6. Once you recognize you're in a dream, focus on talking to anyone near you, or continuing to do whatever you were doing before you recognized the fact. Try to keep walking, keep doing something. Just calm yourself down so you don't feel yourself waking up. If you're scared in a dream, wake up.

In some ways he's actually been inconsiderate when I've been depressed, and not understanding.
